## How to reach IIT Madras

```{=html}
<div class="qgrid qgrid-2">
  <div class="qcard travel">
    <h4>By air</h4>
    <ul class="ilist">
      <li><b>Airport</b><a href="https://www.aai.aero/en/airports/chennai">Chennai International Airport (MAA)</a>, about <strong>14 km</strong> from IIT Madras</li>
      <li><b>Taxi</b>Uber, Ola, Rapido and prepaid taxis pick up passengers at the multi-level car park in the <strong>Aerohub West</strong> building. The drive to the campus takes about <strong>30 to 45 minutes</strong></li>
      <li><b>Metro</b>From the airport station to <strong>Guindy</strong> on <a href="https://chennaimetrorail.org/">Chennai Metro</a>, then a short taxi ride</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="qcard travel">
    <h4>By train or bus</h4>
    <ul class="ilist">
      <li><b>Chennai Central (MAS)</b>Connected to major cities across India. About 30 to 45 minutes to the campus by taxi or auto-rickshaw</li>
      <li><b>Chennai Egmore (MS)</b>Mainly serves Tamil Nadu and neighboring states. About 20 to 30 minutes to the campus</li>
      <li><b>Interstate buses</b>Arrive at the Kalaignar Centenary Bus Terminus or at the Chennai Mofussil Bus Terminus (CMBT), Koyambedu</li>
      <li><b>Onward</b>Take a taxi or auto-rickshaw from the station or bus terminus to the campus</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="qcard travel travel-wide">
  <h4>Getting to the campus</h4>
  <ul class="ilist ilist-2">
    <li><b>Main gate</b>On <strong>Sardar Patel Road</strong>, Adyar</li>
    <li><b>Metro</b>Nearest station is <strong>Guindy</strong>, a short taxi or auto-rickshaw ride away</li>
    <li><b>City buses</b>Stops at Adyar Gate and CLRI</li>
    <li><b>On campus</b>Shuttle buses run from the main gate. The security staff can guide you to the ICSR Building</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

We will share the details directly with the speakers and their group members. We request all other participants to **make their own arrangements**. For the **hostel rooms** reserved for selected PhD students and postdocs, see the [Application](application.html#accommodation) page.

## Sightseeing in and around Chennai

Chennai and its surroundings offer a rich mix of **history, culture and coastline**. Distances are approximate road distances from the IIT Madras main gate.

```{=html}
<div class="qgrid qgrid-3">
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapaleeshwarar_Temple">
    <span class="dist">8 km</span>
    <h4>Kapaleeshwarar Temple</h4>
    <p>A temple dedicated to Shiva in Mylapore, one of the oldest neighborhoods of Chennai, known for its tall, richly sculpted gopuram in the Dravidian style.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Thomas_Cathedral_Basilica,_Chennai">
    <span class="dist">9 km</span>
    <h4>Santhome Basilica</h4>
    <p>A neo-Gothic cathedral built over the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle, one of only three churches in the world built over the tomb of an apostle.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marina_Beach">
    <span class="dist">10 km</span>
    <h4>Marina Beach</h4>
    <p>One of the longest urban beaches in the world, stretching about 13 km along the Bay of Bengal. Best visited early in the morning or in the evening.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_St._George,_India">
    <span class="dist">14 km</span>
    <h4>Fort St. George</h4>
    <p>Founded in 1639, the first English fortress in India. Today it houses the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and the Fort Museum.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DakshinaChitra">
    <span class="dist">26 km</span>
    <h4>DakshinaChitra</h4>
    <p>A living museum of South Indian art, crafts and heritage on the East Coast Road, with traditional homes from Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_Monuments_at_Mahabalipuram">
    <span class="dist">49 km</span>
    <h4>Mahabalipuram</h4>
    <p>A UNESCO World Heritage Site with Pallava monuments from the 7th and 8th centuries, including the Shore Temple, cave temples and monumental bas-reliefs.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanchipuram">
    <span class="dist">74 km</span>
    <h4>Kanchipuram</h4>
    <p>One of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism, known for its many ancient Dravidian temples and its handwoven silk sarees.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vedanthangal_Bird_Sanctuary">
    <span class="dist">82 km</span>
    <h4>Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary</h4>
    <p>One of the oldest bird sanctuaries in India. Large numbers of migratory water birds can be seen here until March.</p>
  </a>
  <a class="qcard place" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pondicherry">
    <span class="dist">140 km</span>
    <h4>Pondicherry</h4>
    <p>A former French colony on the Bay of Bengal, known for the tree-lined streets and colonial architecture of White Town, its seaside promenade and nearby Auroville.</p>
  </a>
</div>
```
